notes:
Read from all thirteen pages at tests/fixtures/catalogue_pipeline/avm_consumables/: 460 rows across 48 sections, all conforming with nothing held (tests/test_avm_consumables_contract.py). AVM's THIRD document, and the one originally asked for on 2026-09-01 before the VetriScience list took its place.

STILL OPEN at the time this was marked SUPPORTED:
  * NO GOLDEN COVERAGE. The sample sheet's eighteen AVM rows are VetriScience supplements; not one of these 460 appears on it. The read rests on the document alone.
  * THE CODE IS THE MANUFACTURER'S, not necessarily AVM's. It is printed in brackets at the end of the description — NG622 is Mila's, J322a2 is the stain maker's — and 267 of the 460 rows carry one. Good enough to match on; worth confirming with AVM before it is trusted as the identifier on an invoice, which is exactly what a three-way match would rely on.
  * 193 rows carry no code at all and take their identity at the match, per the 2026-08-26 ruling.
  * Only a bracketed token containing a DIGIT is read as a code. The same brackets hold colours and dimensions — (Blue), (Orange), (22in) — and a tube whose supplier code read 'Blue' would match confidently against nothing.
  * The page states no basis; PACK on the 2026-09-03 ruling.
  * Dated 20 October 2025 and read on 2026-09-06. Whether these are current prices is a question for AVM.

expected_semantics.reason: Three facts in one column, and the contract reads two of them out. The code NG622 comes from the brackets at the end; only a bracketed token carrying a digit qualifies, which is what stops '(22in)' in the same row becoming the code. No pack is stated, so this is one tube — and '6Fr x 55cm' is the tube's gauge and length, never a quantity of tubes.

The row that shows why the code pattern demands a digit. '(Orange)' is the cap colour and must not become this tube's supplier code — a wrong code matches confidently against the wrong thing, which is worse than no code, and this row correctly yields none. The pack does read: HK$270.00 buys a hundred tubes, HK$2.70 each. The '1.3ml' beside it is what one tube holds and is not a count.
